story: Gary is standing at the bulletin board on Magnolia Loop, reading the Architectural Review notice with a determined squint, while the breeze tugs at the paper and the November sun warms the golf carts parked along the curb. Donna is hurrying down the street from her house, eager to see what Gary has found, and Hal is coming along right behind her with the resolute stride of a man who has already made up his mind. Back in her kitchen, Rosa is content to stay put, finishing tonight's dinner menu and writing out a grocery list for all three neighbors.
events: Gary (street bulletin board): Read the Architectural Review notice for where to submit and the next meeting date
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Finish the dinner menu and write out the grocery list for all three neighbors

gary.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with the Architectural Review form filled out and measurements double-checked. Last tick I checked the bulletin board, but nothing came of it in my notes, so I should look again at the actual posting for the submission details and meeting dates. No one's around, so it's a quiet moment to get this sorted. Rules matter here: I'd rather get the paperwork done right so the lights and speakers pass before Tuesday's pickleball.

parameters.content: Read the Architectural Review notice for where to submit and the next meeting date

donna.thought_process: I've already texted Gary twice about Tuesday pickleball and packed the bag with a spare beginner paddle. The court booking is at the two-hour max, so I'm within L-05. Nobody's around to talk to, and it's nearly noon on a Tuesday, so it's time to stop fussing and get to the courts. Gary has never played, so I'll want to be there first, set up, and let him see how fun it is before he can back out. Heading out the door onto Magnolia Loop is the next step.

parameters.content: Heading out with my pickleball bag to meet Gary at the courts for our Tuesday game.

hal.thought_process: The tally is counted, the notebook is written up, citing L-01 and L-02, and nobody's around to distract me. A report sitting in a notebook doesn't enforce anything. The committee needs it in their hands, and Town Hall is the place to file it. Magnolia Loop is the only way out of the house, so I head that direction. Gary and Donna are decent neighbors, but order is order, and I'll file it plain and fair, no embellishment.

parameters.content: Heading out with my finished tally and notes to get the report to the review committee.

rosa.thought_process: I'm alone at home at 11 AM on a Tuesday. Thursday 8 AM is already inked in for coffee with Hal, and the shift schedule is handled. Last tick I started planning the next dinner menu and grocery list in the kitchen. My goal is a welcome dinner with all three neighbors at one table, and Gary and Donna already came once. The kitchen is the next real step, so I should finish the menu and write the list rather than recheck the schedule again.

parameters.content: Finish the dinner menu and write out the grocery list for all three neighbors

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
